instructions: Pour 3 cups of water into the pot of a puttu steamer and bring it to a boil over high heat while you prepare the flour.
In a large bowl, mix the puttu flour with the salt. Add 1/4 cup water and crumble it with your fingertips.
Keep adding water a little at a time, up to about 1 cup in all, and mixing, until the flour looks like damp sand.
Squeeze a handful. It should hold together in your fist and crumble when you press it. Break up any lumps with your fingers.
Fill the puttu tube with a quarter of the coconut and a quarter of the flour in layers: coconut, flour, coconut, flour, coconut. Start and end with coconut. Fill it loosely and level the top.
Close the tube and set it on the pot of boiling water. Steam for about 5 minutes, until steam comes out of the holes in the top.
Take the tube off the pot and let it rest for 2 minutes. Push the puttu out from the back with a wooden spoon.
Repeat with the rest of the flour and coconut to make 4 puttu in all. Serve hot with the sliced ripe bananas.
method_notes: Hebbar's Kitchen leads (5 stars from 262): damp puttu flour layered with grated coconut in a puttu tube and steamed for about 5 minutes. Lathi's Kitchen (5 from 35) uses the same method with a plain rice flour and warm water. Both serve it with kadala curry or ripe banana; only the banana is written here, as no source gives a kadala curry for this dish. It needs a puttu maker, a tube set on a steamer pot, and with one tube the four puttu take about 30 minutes.
